packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. I did nothing beyond the brief, except that I used `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- There are two faces of one narrow horizontal strip, about 17 cm x 4 cm, cut from a two-column page. Face A: overview image-001, tiles image-002 (left column) and image-003 (right column). Face B: overview image-004, tiles image-005 (left column) and image-006 (right column).
- Each face shows 8 to 9 lines of two columns in a small gothic textualis, brown ink, ruled in plumbet or drypoint. A horizontal fold or crease runs near line 2/3 of each face, with sewing holes along it (binding reuse). The top and bottom lines are cut through. I see no rubrics, initials or glosses on this strip.
- The content looks like continuous prose with citations of authorities, with references such as "ep(isto)la .lv.", "li. iiij.", "Sen(eca) ep(isto)la .ix.". Tentative interpretation: a moral or preaching treatise or compilation on avarice (auaritia recurs). No work or author is identified.
- Selected: all visible lines of all four column fragments. Unread: the partially cut top line of each column and the cut bottom line.

TRANSCRIPTION
The lines are numbered from the top of each tile. Overviews image-001/004 duplicate the tiles and are not counted separately.

== Face A, left column (image-002) ==

l.2  preciu(m)? ?iam? ad pedes ap(osto)lo(rum) ad ostendend(um)
l.3  auaritiam e(ss)e calcanda(m) . Ca(n)o(n)? narrat   [last word ?narrat / ?narrare]
l.4  Sen(eca) . li . iiij . de b(e)n(e)f(i)ci(is)? / ?de filiis? q(uo)m(odo)? ?om(n)ib(us)? de auaritia
l.5  ?Solentium? / ?Sollicitum? ?tiam? ad q(ui)etu(m)? ?n(on)? aut(em) .
l.6  quecu(m)q(ue)? quid? tanta ?uelocitas? / ?uetitas? ?l(?)? ?uie? ?ad?
l.7  ?hanc? ?arcta? ut ?incuruaret? & ?defoderet?
l.8  ?tissimu(m)? ?telluris? intime se ?ingeret?
l.9  [cut: tops of letters only] [illegible]

l.7  intulit . & multa ?con?(cupis)? concupiscendo

LIMITATIONS
- The strip is cut at top and bottom. Line 1 and the last line of each column are partial. The crease at about line 2/3 has a stain and holes, and the readings on the crease are weakest (face B left column l.3, face A right column l.3).
- Which face is recto, and the order of columns across the faces, cannot be determined from the strip. A face A/B continuity cannot be established from these lines.
- Abbreviation expansions are tentative, especially for the citation numerals ("lv", "iiij", "ix", "xviij").
- An adjacent strip from the same leaf, if one exists, would supply the missing lines.
